# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
...

-- A person's plans: an amount (0.00 or more, two decimals), a start date, every N days (at least 1) and an end date
-- (not before the start). Generating makes a DRAFT claim for each plan date (the start, then every N days) up to the
-- end and the sheet's today that has none yet.
CREATE TABLE plan (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    amount DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL,
    start_date DATE NOT NULL,
    every_days INT NOT NULL,
    end_date DATE NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX plan_sheet ON plan (sheet_id, id);
-- The claims a plan has made: one per plan date at most.
CREATE TABLE plan_claim (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    plan_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES plan (id),
    on_date DATE NOT NULL,
    claim_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES claim (id)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX plan_claim_plan_date ON plan_claim (plan_id, on_date);
-- A plan may instead run monthly on a day of the month (1 to 31): its dates are that day in every month from the
-- start's month (a day beyond the month's length falls on its last day), dates before the start left out. A monthly
-- plan has a month day and no every N days; any other plan has every N days and no month day.
ALTER TABLE plan ALTER COLUMN every_days SET NULL;
ALTER TABLE plan ADD COLUMN month_day INT;
-- A plan's pauses: paused on a day (the sheet's today) and resumed on a later one (null while it is still paused).
-- A plan date on or after the day it was paused and before the day it was resumed is skipped, not postponed.
CREATE TABLE plan_pause (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    plan_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES plan (id),
    paused_on DATE NOT NULL,
    resumed_on DATE
);
CREATE INDEX plan_pause_plan ON plan_pause (plan_id, id);

-- A person's plans: an amount (0.00 or more, two decimals), a start date, every N days (at least 1) and an end date
-- (not before the start). Generating makes a DRAFT claim for each plan date (the start, then every N days) up to the
-- end and the sheet's today that has none yet.
CREATE TABLE plan (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sheet_id VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL REFERENCES sheet (id),
    person_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES person (id),
    amount DECIMAL(19, 2) NOT NULL,
    start_date DATE NOT NULL,
    every_days INT NOT NULL,
    end_date DATE NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX plan_sheet ON plan (sheet_id, id);
-- The claims a plan has made: one per plan date at most.
CREATE TABLE plan_claim (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    plan_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES plan (id),
    on_date DATE NOT NULL,
    claim_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES claim (id)
);
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX plan_claim_plan_date ON plan_claim (plan_id, on_date);
-- A plan may instead run monthly on a day of the month (1 to 31): its dates are that day in every month from the
-- start's month (a day beyond the month's length falls on its last day), dates before the start left out. A monthly
-- plan has a month day and no every N days; any other plan has every N days and no month day.
ALTER TABLE plan ALTER COLUMN every_days SET NULL;
ALTER TABLE plan ADD COLUMN month_day INT;
-- A plan's pauses: paused on a day (the sheet's today) and resumed on a later one (null while it is still paused).
-- A plan date on or after the day it was paused and before the day it was resumed is skipped, not postponed.
CREATE TABLE plan_pause (
    id BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    plan_id BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES plan (id),
    paused_on DATE NOT NULL,
    resumed_on DATE
);
CREATE INDEX plan_pause_plan ON plan_pause (plan_id, id);

You can now change a plan's amount, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**One thing to check:** the spec types into `plan-amount`, but that test id was already on a read-only span showing the amount. I turned that span into a text field pre-filled with the current amount, so the test id keeps its name. Anything that read the amount as the element's text, rather than as the field's value, will no longer see it. Nothing in the current spec reads it that way.

**How it behaves**
- Each plan row has the amount field and a `plan-amount-save` button. Saving does three things:
  - It sets the plan's amount, so claims generated from then on use it. Claims already generated keep their amount.
  - It records the change with the sheet's today.
  - It writes `PLAN_CHANGED sheet=… by=… name=<person> start=<plan start> amount=<new amount>` to the audit file.
- A bad amount (one that isn't 0.00 or more with up to two decimals, e.g. `1.005`) is refused. It shows `plan-error` and writes nothing.
- Each plan lists its changes oldest first as `plan-change-line` items in the form `<date> amount=<amount>`.

**Where it lives**
- **Data:** a new table, `V95__plan_change.sql`, holds the plan id, the date and the amount.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans/{planId}/amount`, built the same way as pause/resume. The plans list now includes each plan's changes.
- **Front end:** the field, button, error and change list are in `features/plans/person.slot.tsx`.

**Beyond what the test checks:** transferring a person to another sheet re-creates their plans there and deletes the originals. It now carries each plan's amount changes across too. Without that, the transfer would fail for any plan that had changes.
